empirical.title: Suicidality in the MENAT region: A systematic review and meta-analysis
empirical.keyFindings: Pooled prevalence: Ideation (25%), Attempts (12%). Associations: Anxiety (OR=3.1) and Loneliness (OR=2.2)

empirical.title: Mechanisms linking childhood socioeconomic disadvantage to adolescent gun violence
empirical.keyFindings: SED associated with gun violence (beta = .468, p = .011); double mediation through conduct problems and deviant peers

empirical.title: Adverse childhood experiences and violent behavior in non-incarcerated adults
empirical.keyFindings: Severe multi-type adversity increased violence risk (OR = 8.07)

empirical.title: Role of genotype in the cycle of violence in maltreated children
empirical.keyFindings: Low-activity MAOA variants showed higher violent offending only when paired with abuse

empirical.title: Rising temperatures and violence worldwide
empirical.keyFindings: +1°C = 1.64% increase in violent events; effect specific to interpersonal violence

empirical.title: Risk factors for suicide mortality in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis
empirical.keyFindings: Strongest associations: Mental disorder (OR=13.1) and self-harm history (OR=10.1)

empirical.title: Effectiveness of universal violence prevention
empirical.keyFindings: Strongest effects: Sports-based/martial arts programs (OR=2.66)

empirical.title: Replicating Sampson and Groves's test of social disorganization theory
empirical.source: Journal of Research in Crime and Delinquency
empirical.keyFindings: Unsupervised peer groups strongly predicted victimization (r = .40)

empirical.title: MAOA gene interaction with violence
empirical.keyFindings: Genetic moderation emerged only after specific threshold of maltreatment

empirical.title: Prefrontal brain abnormalities in antisocial individuals: A meta-analysis
empirical.keyFindings: Significant prefrontal reduction in antisocial groups (d = -0.60)

empirical.title: Risk factors for violence in psychosis: Systematic review
empirical.keyFindings: Criminal history (OR = 3.1) and hostile behavior (p < .001) were strong predictors

empirical.title: Colonial legacy and contemporary civil violence
empirical.keyFindings: Path-dependent imprints of colonial administrative styles predict modern civil violence patterns

empirical.title: ACEs among justice-involved youth
empirical.keyFindings: 87% ACE prevalence among justice-involved youth

empirical.authors: Choi, H. M., Lee, W., Roye, D., et al.
empirical.title: Temperature, crime, and violence: A systematic review and meta-analysis
empirical.keyFindings: Comprehensive meta-analysis confirming temperature-violence association; high temperatures increase crime and violence across contexts

empirical.authors: Sampson, R. J., & Groves, W. B.
empirical.title: Community structure and crime: Testing social-disorganization theory
empirical.keyFindings: β = .35 for unsupervised peer groups → street robbery; structural conditions mediate poverty-crime link through friendship networks, organizational participation, and peer supervision (N=238 British communities)

empirical.authors: Sampson, R. J., Raudenbush, S. W., & Earls, F.
empirical.title: Neighborhoods and violent crime: A multilevel study of collective efficacy
empirical.keyFindings: β = −0.45 collective efficacy → perceived violence; 2-SD elevation in collective efficacy → 39.7% reduction in expected homicide rate (N=8,782 residents, 343 Chicago neighborhoods, PHDCN)

empirical.authors: Papachristos, A. V., Braga, A. A., & Hureau, D. M.
empirical.title: Social networks and the risk of gunshot injury
empirical.keyFindings: OR = 0.754 per network degree of separation (25% reduction per step); 85% of gunshot injuries in one network component (N=763, Boston Cape Verdean community)

empirical.title: Network exposure and homicide victimization in an African American community
empirical.keyFindings: OR = 0.430 per network degree (57% reduction per step); homicide rate 900% higher for network members (554 vs. 55 per 100,000); 41% of homicides in <4% of population (N=3,718, Chicago 2006-2011)

empirical.authors: Papachristos, A. V., Wildeman, C., & Roberto, E.
empirical.title: Tragic, but not random: The social contagion of nonfatal gunshot injuries
empirical.keyFindings: OR = 3.13 at 1 degree of exposure; 70% of nonfatal gunshots in networks comprising <6% of city population; rate 740 vs. 62 per 100,000 citywide (N=169,620, Chicago 2006-2012)

empirical.authors: Green, B., Horel, T., & Papachristos, A. V.
empirical.title: Modeling contagion through social networks to explain and predict gunshot violence in Chicago, 2006 to 2014
empirical.keyFindings: 63.1% of gunshot violence episodes attributable to social contagion; combined contagion + demographics model identifies 53.3% more subjects than demographics alone at top 1% daily risk (N=138,163, Chicago 2006-2014)

empirical.title: Connected in crime: The enduring effect of neighborhood networks on the spatial patterning of violence
empirical.keyFindings: Co-offending networks among 172,714 individuals link all Chicago neighborhoods; network models outperform spatial adjacency for crime distribution; networks generated by concentrated disadvantage and collective efficacy deficits

empirical.authors: Lotto, C. R., Barlow, J., & Pinto, R. J.
empirical.title: Maternal history of childhood adversities and later negative parenting: A systematic review
empirical.keyFindings: Maternal childhood adversity associated with negative parenting behaviors including harsh discipline and reduced sensitivity; intergenerational transmission pathway

empirical.title: Alcohol, drugs, and violence: A meta-meta-analysis
empirical.keyFindings: 72% correlation between substance misuse and violence; meta-meta-analysis synthesizing prior meta-analyses on substance-violence link

empirical.title: The effect of media violence on aggression: A meta-analysis and test of replicability
empirical.keyFindings: Meta-analysis of publications from 1963-2023 testing replicability of media violence effect on aggression
